title: Compiler diagnostics are structured only at the external CLI boundary
observed_need: Compile-fail and diagnostic tests must match diagnostic identity and preserve source spans without scraping human prose.
current_language_behavior: The Rust toolchain exposes versioned structured diagnostics and the native runner fail-closes on invalid admission. P-062 added a Test-owned MNCS application that projects diagnostic codes and applies compile verdict policy without building a host diagnostic-code list. P-063 replaces the verdict application's Test JsonValue tree projection with bounded Stdlib JSON cursor events and a syntax validator. P-064 added bounded native typed records for standard diagnostic objects; P-065 extended them with expected tokens and one level of related diagnostics. P-066 replaced the diagnostic projector's JsonValue tree traversal with a second bounded json_cursor pass over the original chunked bytes. P-067 retires the fixed native diagnostic-record output array and Python reconstruction mapper: MNCS validates the selected array and returns its source span, then Python decodes only that span for the public dictionary contract. P-068 removes the redundant per-field typed validation buffers; the native cursor now validates JSON and selection metadata, bounds the selected array, and preserves arbitrary diagnostic JSON values in the selected span. P-069 initially fed the selected span through the Test-owned MNCS JSON token tape, where Python assembled public lists and dictionaries from native structural events. P-070 replaces that compile-entry projection with bounded typed diagnostic-code values plus the selected diagnostic-array source span from the native verdict application. Python decodes only code bytes for compile policy and carries the diagnostic array opaquely into the native public-result key-order and window formatter; it does not build diagnostic lists or dictionaries on the ordinary supported path. The formatter emits 4,096-byte windows and carries source SHA-256 state across continuations, checking the full input digest on the final window rather than rehashing it on every call. The 29,188-byte nested differential case completed in ten native calls with its 37,377-byte output and digest matching the independent golden under the existing step ceiling. The native_compile_diagnostic_records helper materializes records only for Python API-boundary callers. MNCS application code still cannot directly consume compiler Diagnostic values. P-071 removes the last supported-path code-list projection from Python: the native verdict app canonicalizes observed code values into a bounded JSON array carried in at most sixteen 1,024-byte chunks. Python validates chunk lengths and joins opaque bytes, then inserts the fragment only for diagnostic-mismatch results; compile-policy code comparison remains native. Escaped code strings and multi-chunk output match independent expectations. P-072 folds diagnostic-array span selection into the existing compile-verdict cursor scan and retires the standalone second pass. A 16,384-byte valid compiler document exhausted the unchanged 8,000,000-step cap before the fusion; it now completes with the expected verdict and exact diagnostic span under that same cap. P-073 raises the native document ceiling from 16,384 to 18,000 bytes within the unchanged 8,000,000-step run-app cap. The 18,000-byte differential input returns its expected verdict and exact span; 18,432-byte, 32,768-byte, and 65,536-byte probes exhaust that cap, so the adapter keeps larger documents on the atomic compatibility path.
why_insufficient: The bounded native path keeps diagnostics and observed-code arrays as native JSON fragments through result assembly, and one cursor scan validates, selects the span, and gathers policy codes. The native document ceiling is 18,000 bytes under the existing 8,000,000-step run-app cap. Unsupported shapes, excessive nesting, over-bound values, native budget exhaustion, and larger documents still use the atomic Python JSON compatibility parser. The explicit native_compile_diagnostic_records API wrapper still materializes a selected array when a caller requests dictionaries, and Test still cannot consume compiler Diagnostic values directly.
minimal_reproducer: tests/fixtures/compile_fail.mncs plus tools/mncs_test.py: compile_entry sends compiler output to the native diagnostic verdict and span applications, carries selected diagnostics and observed-code JSON fragments opaquely into the Test public-result serializer, and uses native values for failure policy.
desired_direction: A versioned diagnostic value/protocol exposing code, severity, source span, related diagnostics, and rendered forms to native tooling.
workaround: The Test-owned MNCS diagnostic application validates the compiler JSON, applies compile-verdict policy, emits canonical observed-code JSON in bounded chunks, and returns the selected diagnostic-array span while the same cursor pass gathers policy codes. The 18,000-byte input ceiling completes within the unchanged 8,000,000-step run-app limit. Larger input probes exhaust that limit, so oversized and unsupported documents use the full Python compatibility parser atomically. Python otherwise concatenates only native code-fragment bytes and preserves the fragments through the public-result formatter. No formatted-stderr parsing is used.
